pages.title: Install and run
pages.description: Build or launch Opute Host Agent locally with explicit identity, authentication, and safe loopback defaults.
pages.body: How-to Install & run Choose a local source build or the published npm launcher. For a tested end-to-end setup, begin with the first-success tutorial . From source From the Host Agent repository root, build and start the standalone HTTP server. Host inspection does not require Incus or Kubernetes. make build VERSION=0.2.2 export OPUTE_REMOTE_AGENT_ID="local-$(openssl rand -hex 8)" export MCP_AUTH_TOKEN="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" ./dist/opute-host-agent serve --mode standalone --transport http Keep both values in your local shell. The agent ID is an explicit opaque identity; the launcher does not invent a default. The token authenticates MCP requests. Published npm launcher export OPUTE_REMOTE_AGENT_ID="local-$(openssl rand -hex 8)" export MCP_AUTH_TOKEN="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" npx -y @opute/host-agent@0.2.1 start --background npx -y @opute/host-agent@0.2.1 url npx -y @opute/host-agent@0.2.1 status npx -y @opute/host-agent@0.2.1 stop This pins the newest published release with a passing read-only package canary. The launcher keeps the explicit identity and token in the child process. Stop the background process when you finish. The compatibility page records verified combinations. Current source candidate: @opute/host-agent@0.2.2 is a preview until its published-package canary passes. The first-success and published launcher instructions above remain pinned to @opute/host-agent@0.2.1 . Local endpoint and modes Mode Default address Purpose standalone 127.0.0.1:3014 Local editor or laptop platform 0.0.0.0:3004 Platform-enrolled host Set HOST_MCP_BIND_HOST and HOST_MCP_PORT when needed. Keep a local tutorial on loopback and use the same port in the agent URL and client configuration. Mutations Standalone mutations are denied by default. This first-success path stays read-only. Only enable OPUTE_STANDALONE_ALLOW_MUTATIONS=true after reviewing the capability effects, approval requirements, and host-local consequences. WSL and production For a first client connection, run the Linux agent and VS Code integration in the same WSL environment. Verify reachability before configuring a client across Windows and WSL. Production hosts are connected through Opute Platform's Connect Remote Host flow. Platform owns enrollment and authorization; use the generated host configuration for that host rather than copying local tutorial credentials. Related: First success · Client configuration · Troubleshooting · Configuration

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.description: Diagnose Host Agent authentication, reachability, identity, discovery, and optional-provider problems.
pages.body: How-to Troubleshooting Use the symptom to identify whether the server is live, the client is authenticated, and the requested provider is available. HTTP 401 from /mcp Confirm MCP_AUTH_TOKEN is set in the Host Agent process environment. Confirm the client sends Authorization: Bearer with that same token. Use the local check in the first-success tutorial to verify that a wrong token returns 401 and the correct token can call get_host_info . GET /health is intentionally open. A successful health response proves liveness, not that MCP authentication works. Connection refused or the wrong port Standalone defaults to http://127.0.0.1:3014/mcp . Use the same value for HOST_MCP_PORT , the health URL, and the client's MCP URL. Keep HOST_MCP_BIND_HOST=127.0.0.1 for a local client. Check that the port is free and the server is still running. For Windows/WSL, first verify the client can reach an agent running in the same WSL distribution. Missing OPUTE_REMOTE_AGENT_ID Set one explicit opaque ID before starting the process. The npm launcher fails before binary download or listener startup when it is absent; it does not default to a shared name. Do not use the local daemon ownership ID as the Host Agent identity. The client connects but the tool list is empty or stale Refresh the client's MCP tools after connecting. The live tools/list response is authoritative. Check that the client is connected to the same host and port where /health reports the expected agentId . Review the current capability reference ; provider readiness varies by host. An optional provider tool is unavailable Host facts do not require Incus or Kubernetes. VM inventory requires an Incus provider; cluster discovery requires the relevant Kubernetes provider and host access. A listed tool does not prove the provider service is ready. Mutation denied Standalone mode denies mutating tools unless OPUTE_STANDALONE_ALLOW_MUTATIONS=true is explicitly enabled. Keep it disabled during the first-success tutorial. Platform-enrolled hosts use Platform authorization policy. Launcher status does not match the health response The launcher uses localInstanceId to identify its managed local process. agentId is the canonical Host Agent identity and instanceId describes the execution mode; these fields have separate meanings. Related: Install and run · Client setup · Configuration · Resources & safety

pages.title: How this site is hosted
pages.description: Understand the public image build and the private Host Agent deployment controller that serves Opute's website.
pages.body: How-to How this site is hosted The public repository builds a static-site image. A private deployment controller selects that image and asks the local Host Agent to deploy it through typed capabilities. Ownership boundary Public Host Agent source owns the website, docs generator, and GitHub-hosted image build. Its workflow publishes an immutable image digest without Host Agent deployment credentials. Private site deployment owns source-run selection, the controller, deployment recipe, and private rollout evidence. This repository is required to operate or change production deployment. Opute Platform and its MCP endpoint remain separate services with their own owners and route checks. Delivery path flowchart LR Source[Public website source] --> Build[Public image build] Build -->|verified run and digest| Registry[Public image registry] Controller[Private deployment controller] -->|select successful source run| Registry Controller --> Recipe[Typed Host Agent recipe] Recipe --> Agent[Local Host Agent] Agent --> Workload[Website workload] Workload --> Routes[www and apex routes] Browser[Visitor] --> Routes Diagram in words: Public CI builds and publishes the website image. A private controller verifies and selects that image, then uses a typed Host Agent recipe to update the website workload behind the two public website routes. What deployment evidence means The private recipe finishes successfully and the serving workload uses the selected image digest with a Ready Pod. Both www.opute.io and opute.io serve rendered pages and a /build.json marker matching the selected source SHA, run ID, and attempt. Critical docs routes, static assets, and search load and return useful content; HTTP 200 by itself does not prove that the client onboarding path works. platform.opute.io and authenticated mcp.opute.io are checked separately and remain outside this site's deployment boundary. These checks establish evidence for a particular rollout. They do not create an uptime, high availability, or successful client-onboarding guarantee. Rollback and credentials Rollback uses the private controller's explicit selection of a previous successful public source run and repeats the deployment and route gates. Public site workflows do not contain deployment credentials; Host Agent and tunnel credentials remain in their owning runtime. See the private deployment repository for current operating instructions. This public page describes ownership and evidence, not a direct infrastructure procedure.

pages.title: Get started
pages.description: Start Opute Host Agent on Linux and verify authenticated MCP tool discovery.
pages.body: Tutorial Get started Outcome. Start Host Agent locally, connect VS Code over authenticated HTTP, refresh the live tool list, and read host facts with get_host_info {} . This tutorial does not enable mutations. Verified release. This path pins @opute/host-agent@0.2.1 ; its published authenticated read-only canary passed for catalog revision sha256:1efa6beb86423ee9fe3f1e71f978958566950726f45dcc5d21743711135e2b91 . View this exact capability snapshot or download its JSON . Prerequisites Linux or WSL2, Node.js 18 or newer, npm, and VS Code with HTTP MCP support. curl and openssl ; loopback port 3014 must be free. Network access to npm and the matching Linux binary in GitHub Releases . Start the local agent Set an explicit identity and random secret Keep the token in your shell and VS Code prompt. Do not commit it or put it in screenshots. export OPUTE_REMOTE_AGENT_ID="local-$(openssl rand -hex 8)" export MCP_AUTH_TOKEN="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" npx -y @opute/host-agent@0.2.1 start --background This starts the pinned published package shown on this page. Stop the background process with npx -y @opute/host-agent@0.2.1 stop. curl -i -sS http://127.0.0.1:3014/health Expect HTTP 200 and the exact agentId you set. This open endpoint proves liveness only, not MCP authentication. Connect VS Code Create .vscode/mcp.json . VS Code documents this HTTP server and password-prompt setup in its MCP configuration reference . { "inputs": [{"type":"promptString","id":"opute-host-token","description":"Local Opute Host Agent token","password":true}], "servers": {"opute-host-agent":{"type":"http","url":"http://127.0.0.1:3014/mcp","headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer ${input:opute-host-token}"}}} } Start the server and enter the same shell token. Avoid committing the config if the client might persist the entered value. Refresh tools and read the host Confirm the server is connected, refresh its tools, and call get_host_info with {} . Its schema requires these host facts: { "uri": "host:example:host-01", "hostName": "…", "providerId": "…", "lxcBinaryPath": "…", "systemctlPath": "…", "supportedTools": ["…"] } Those six fields are required by the current schema. Optional fields such as agent , capacity , and system appear only when observable. Values are redacted; this is an example shape, not captured host output. A listed capability does not prove its provider is ready. Keep this first check read-only. Do not set OPUTE_STANDALONE_ALLOW_MUTATIONS=true or call a tool whose declared effect is not read . Verify the authenticated path Check that authentication rejects a deliberately wrong token before completing the valid call in VS Code: curl -i -sS http://127.0.0.1:3014/mcp -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer intentionally-wrong' --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}' Expect HTTP 401. A request with no Authorization header also returns 401. Use the real token only in your local shell and VS Code password prompt. No token or a wrong token gets HTTP 401. The configured token connects VS Code; non-empty tools/list includes get_host_info . get_host_info {} returns structured facts and the selected identity. No mutation flag was enabled and no mutating tool was called. Troubleshoot Port in use: Check the launcher with npx -y @opute/host-agent@0.2.1 status, stop it if needed, then choose an unused HOST_MCP_PORT and use that same port in curl and VS Code. 401: match the VS Code input to MCP_AUTH_TOKEN ; restart after changing shell environment. Empty tools: refresh the server, verify the URL ends in /mcp , and check tools/list . WSL reachability: run VS Code and the agent in the same WSL context first. For other symptoms, see troubleshooting . Next Inspect list_vms only if Incus is configured. Otherwise read the capability reference and product boundary . Keep the mutation gate closed.

pages.title: Connect an MCP client
pages.description: Configure VS Code to connect to a local Opute Host Agent over authenticated Streamable HTTP.
pages.body: How-to Connect an MCP client Connect VS Code to a Host Agent running in the same Linux or WSL context. The documented path uses Streamable HTTP and a password-prompted Bearer token. VS Code Start Host Agent on loopback and retain MCP_AUTH_TOKEN in the same shell. Create a workspace .vscode/mcp.json with an HTTP MCP server and a password input: { "inputs": [{"type":"promptString","id":"opute-host-token","description":"Local Opute Host Agent token","password":true}], "servers": {"opute-host-agent":{"type":"http","url":"http://127.0.0.1:3014/mcp","headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer ${input:opute-host-token}"}}} } Start the server from VS Code and enter the local token at its prompt. Refresh tools and call get_host_info {} to confirm the authenticated path. See the official VS Code MCP configuration reference . This site has not yet recorded a human client run for a specific VS Code release; see compatibility evidence . WSL and local networking Keep the editor MCP client and Host Agent in a networking context where 127.0.0.1:3014 reaches the agent. Start with both in the same WSL distribution. If VS Code runs on Windows while the agent runs in WSL, follow the editor's current WSL integration guidance and verify connectivity before configuring MCP. Other clients Other clients must support Streamable HTTP MCP and the required Bearer header for this setup. Client-specific recipes are not published as tested until a named version completes the read-only canary. Next: complete the full first-success tutorial .

pages.title: Use cases
pages.description: See how Opute Host Agent configures K3s clusters, verifies membership, and exposes read-only host facts.
pages.body: Use cases Configure, verify, then inspect Host Agent exposes typed operations through authenticated MCP. Available workflows depend on the live catalog and configured providers. Read the current catalog before acting; it is a capability description, not proof that a provider is ready. Understand the connected host Call get_host_info {} to read the host URI, hostname, provider identity, and supported tools. Use this result to confirm which Host Agent answered before asking for a resource inventory. Discover operations available now Call get_capability_catalog {} and inspect its revision and declared effect. Refresh tools/list after connecting; live discovery is authoritative for that process. Inspect VM inventory when Incus is configured Call list_vms only on a host with its Incus provider available. This is inventory discovery; creating, changing, or deleting a guest is a separate mutating operation and is outside the first-success tutorial. Discover Kubernetes clusters when configured Use list_kubernetes_clusters only when the host has an available Kubernetes provider and the intended source is known. An empty inventory and a failed inventory probe are different outcomes; read the structured response and error status. Plan cluster setup and availability Host Agent can provision and configure K3s server membership through typed operations. A local test used 3 Incus server containers with embedded-etcd; after one guest stopped, 2 of 3 Kubernetes nodes remained Ready and a typed API write and read succeeded. Those guests shared one physical host. See the test record and its exact scope . Product boundary. Host Agent executes explicit typed operations against one host. Platform owns intent, authorization, and durable orchestration across hosts. Read how they fit together . This is local dogfood evidence, not a customer outcome, performance result, or availability guarantee. It does not establish physical-host failover, application serving, durable application data, or external endpoint failover. Next: complete the authenticated read-only check or browse the release catalog .

pages.title: Concepts
pages.description: Understand what Opute Host Agent does, how it differs from Opute Platform, and how its typed tools work.
pages.body: Explanation Concepts Opute Host Agent connects authenticated MCP clients to Linux host facts and explicit typed operations. It runs beside a host, applies identity and effect gates, and returns structured observations. Opute Platform coordinates authorized intent and durable work across hosts. For the execution flow and package layout, see Architecture . Host Agent and Platform Host Agent owns execution on one host: it authenticates an MCP client, admits canonical resource URIs, checks typed capability effects, dispatches to the host or an available provider, and returns structured observations. Opute Platform owns intent, authorization, routing, and durable orchestration across hosts. Platform may assign work to a Host Agent; the Host Agent does not become the cross-host coordinator. This website explains and onboards Host Agent. The public Host Agent site uses opute.io and www.opute.io ; Opute Platform has separate platform.opute.io and mcp.opute.io routes. A site deployment does not authorize or mutate those Platform resources. flowchart LR Client[MCP client / Platform] -->|typed tools/list + call| HA[Host Agent] HA -->|ops| Host[Linux host] HA -->|plugins| Prov[Provider MCP processes] Platform[Opute Platform] -->|intent + enrollment| Client Platform -.->|does not own host exec| HA Diagram in words: A local MCP client or Platform sends typed requests to Host Agent. Host Agent executes against its Linux host or provider processes. Platform supplies intent and enrollment context while Host Agent retains host execution. Typed catalog, not folklore Clients do not send free-form shell. They discover a revisioned catalog, validate arguments against schemas, and invoke named tools. That is why memorized tool lists go stale and why tools/list is authoritative. Recipes and plans A recipe is the cookbook page: which dish, which ingredients, which version. A plan is the cooking steps the kitchen actually follows. The Host Agent keeps both so work can be pinned and parameterized, while only one runner ever executes. More: Recipes & plans · field list: primitives . Fail-closed identity Every process must carry a canonical OPUTE_REMOTE_AGENT_ID . Standalone mutations stay off until explicitly enabled. Observations that could contain secrets are redacted in MCP results (write-only schema fields become [redacted] ). Security boundary Treat the Host Agent like an API gateway on the host: authenticate at Streamable HTTP /mcp (Bearer bootstrap and/or OAuth), keep /health unauthenticated for liveness only, and never embed secrets in tool schemas. Prefer live catalog discovery over memorized names. Public dogfood hostnames must not expose Host Agent MCP administration. Providers as plugins Kubernetes, Cloudflare, Tailscale, Ollama, and Host OS surfaces arrive as provider plugins under plugins/ , not as hard-wired product branches inside the MCP server. Shared host seams live in internal/hostruntime ; there is no separate internal/provider package. Optional LLM layer Core infrastructure tools must work when no LLM provider is installed or healthy. LLM serving is an activated capability, not a dependency of the kernel. How this site is written Pages follow Diátaxis : tutorials teach a first success; how-tos accomplish a known goal; reference states facts without narrative; explanation answers why and builds mental models. Mixing those modes produces pages that intimidate without operating — so recipe why lives under Explanation, and the field catalog under Reference.

pages.title: Kubernetes availability
pages.description: Review Opute Host Agent's local K3s setup and one-guest-loss evidence, including what the test does not prove.
pages.body: Explanation Kubernetes availability and failure scope “High availability” is a behavior under a named failure. State which behavior should continue, where the failed component lives, and how recovery works. Verified local Host Agent test · 2026-09-25. Three fresh Incus system container server guests were provisioned and configured through typed Host Agent MCP operations as a K3s v1.31.8+k3s1 cluster with embedded-etcd. The guests shared one physical host. With one guest stopped, 2 of 3 nodes were Ready; a typed ConfigMap apply and read both succeeded through the surviving control plane. Starting the guest restored 3 of 3 Ready nodes. The test used K3s provider 1.0.2 . The Host Agent process reported runtime dev and catalog revision sha256:1399404a31f51c6120e4ea84c5691b61e93a5c4fb23356600bfd28b3aa6f9e2b . The published @opute/host-agent@0.2.1 canary separately proves the authenticated read-only first-success path; it did not test this HA setup flow. This result covers one Incus guest/server failure on one physical host. It does not establish host or site failure recovery, network partition behavior, workload serving, durable application data, new workload scheduling, or external endpoint failover. The membership probe also reported that no external HA endpoint was configured. Separate the outcomes One healthy member list is not an availability test. Check each property that matters to the user: Control-plane writes: can the Kubernetes API accept a change while a server is down? Existing workloads: do already-running Pods continue on a surviving node? New scheduling: can the control plane place or replace workloads? Application serving: does the user-facing endpoint remain reachable? Durable state: does application data remain readable and writable? Record these separately. A service returning HTTP 200 does not prove Kubernetes write availability, and a healthy cluster status does not prove the application path is serving. In this K3s provider, get-cluster-info.readyNodeCount and each node's status expose the per-node observation. Its aggregate ready field is true when at least one node is Ready; that boolean alone does not prove etcd quorum or application health. The typed write and read during the guest failure supply the API write-continuity evidence for this specific test. K3s datastore quorum For embedded etcd, K3s documents an HA cluster as three or more server nodes . Quorum requires a majority. With only two voting members, losing either member removes quorum, so automatic Kubernetes write continuity is not established. With an external datastore, K3s uses two or more server nodes. The external datastore has its own availability requirements and must survive the failure being tested; two K3s servers alone do not make that database highly available. K3s: High Availability Embedded etcd K3s: High Availability External DB Failure domains matter Three guests on one physical computer can demonstrate guest-level setup and failure behavior. They share the computer’s power, storage, host networking, and physical failure domain, so that test cannot establish resilience to losing the host or site. State the tested boundary with the result. What remains untested physical-host or site failure network partition application workload continued serving durable application data survived new workload scheduling during failure external endpoint failover the published npm package HA setup path What a clean setup test should record Start from isolated hosts with no K3s service, datastore, or prior cluster membership. If the claim includes installing and enrolling Host Agent itself, test that bootstrap as a separate step. Record each exact Host Agent identity, software revision, active provider/catalog revision, and the empty baseline. Use the exact setup capabilities exposed by the tested release. Platform may coordinate authorized cross-host intent and durable runs; each host change should remain attributable to its owning Host Agent. If any setup step uses a shell, CLI, cloud console, or other out-of-band path, record it and narrow the claim: that run did not prove Host Agent-only setup. Verify the expected server membership and the configured datastore mode before injecting failure. Stop or isolate each server in turn. Measure API reads and writes, workload serving, durable application state, and recovery separately. Restore the failed node through the supported typed path, verify it rejoins, and retain redacted run evidence. A successful join proves membership, not clean-room bootstrap or availability. Only the failure checks prove the stated behavior. Use disposable, isolated test hosts for destructive setup and failure injection. Opute ownership boundary Host Agent is the typed executor on one host. Opute Platform owns intent, authorization, routing, and durable orchestration across hosts. A multi-host result must show both the coordinator’s durable outcome and the Host Agent evidence for each affected host. See how the products fit together and how recipes and plans work . This guide states the evidence required for an HA claim. Check the release reference and live tools/list for the capabilities available in a particular installation.

pages.title: Recipes & plans
pages.description: Learn when to use Host Agent recipes or plans and how the runner validates and executes each step.
pages.body: Explanation Recipes & plans About why Host Agent has both recipes and plans — and how to choose a family. Field lists live under Recipe & plan primitives . In one sentence A recipe is the cookbook page (which dish, which ingredients, which version). A plan is the cooking steps the kitchen actually follows. Only the plan runs. flowchart LR Recipe[Recipe envelope] --> Expand[Pin · inputs · expand] Expand --> Plan[host-plan.v1] Plan --> Runner[plan.Runner] Runner --> Tools[Typed tools] Diagram in words: A recipe pins inputs and expands into a host plan. The shared plan runner executes its typed tool steps. Why not one thing? Without recipes, every caller would hand-write expanded plans and lose version pins, input schemas, and family-specific activation. Without plans, each recipe family would invent its own executor — Cordis C-03 forbids that. So recipes package work; plans execute it. Recipe owns identity ( recipeId / recipeVersion ), inputs (including secrets), compatibility, source pin ( sha256 ), and an embedded plan. Plan owns the DAG: nodes, dependsOn, validate/assert, retry, recover, compensate, converge. Bare plans exist when something already expanded the envelope (for example provider teardown returning host-plan.v1 ). Which family when? You want… Use MCP entry Execute a Host Agent-local task (site deployment is controlled by the private repository) host-recipe.v1 local run_host_local_recipe An already-expanded DAG bare host-plan.v1 run_host_plan Activate a serving runtime (LLM, mesh, HTTP exposure) runtime-recipe.v1 run_runtime_recipe Public hostname → local target bindings tunnel-recipe.v1 run_tunnel_recipe Multi-host coordination with waits Platform-distributed host recipe Submit to Platform — HA refuses What the runner is doing After expansion, one runner walks topo levels, applies mutating actions only when readiness fails, can recover then revalidate, and on abort runs compensate in reverse order. Host-local recipes cannot use durable wait nodes — those belong to Platform-distributed work. flowchart TB N[Node] -->|already good| Sat[satisfied] N -->|needs work| Act[action] Act --> Val[validate / assert] Val -->|fail| Rec[recover?] Rec -->|abort| Comp[compensate] Diagram in words: A plan node that is already ready is marked satisfied. Otherwise its action runs, validation checks the result, recovery may retry, and compensation may run if the plan aborts. Where to go next Recipe & plan primitives — every field, status, assertion op, and cap Publish this site — host-local recipe in production Networking — seams recipes compose Resources & safety — redaction and resume

pages.title: Networking
pages.description: Understand Host Agent's membership, private mesh, public ingress, and tunnel capabilities.
pages.body: Explanation Networking HA networking uses three exclusive Service Definitions. mesh-runtime.v1 installs and checks the selected network runtime; the definitions below describe membership, private traffic, and public ingress. Three seams (ADR-0016) Service Definition Job Neutral ops mesh-membership.v1 Host joins a trust domain enroll, status, leave private-mesh.v1 East-west reachability ensure, ensure-service, probe public-ingress.v1 North-south stable HTTPS ensure, promote, probe Legacy network-overlay.* names are deprecated migration aliases. Use mesh-runtime.v1 for network runtime setup and the three Service Definitions in this table for membership, private-mesh, and public-ingress operations. flowchart TB subgraph seams [Service Definitions] M[mesh-membership.v1] Pv[private-mesh.v1] Pu[public-ingress.v1] end TS[Provider: Tailscale all three] CF[Provider: Cloudflare membership + public-ingress] TS --> M TS --> Pv TS --> Pu CF --> M CF --> Pu HA[Host Agent recipes / MCP] --> seams Diagram in words: Tailscale provides membership, private mesh, and public ingress. Cloudflare provides membership and public ingress in the described bundle. Host Agent recipes compose the neutral service definitions. Exclusivity Exclusivity is per Service Definition , not per vendor company. Activating a provider for a definition publishes that definition’s ops and displaces another provider’s catalog entries for the same capabilityId . Ambiguous dual ownership fails closed. v1 vendor-bundle policy: activate one recommended bundle (Tailscale for all three, or Cloudflare where parity exists). Mix-and-match across seams is not a supported product path yet. Private vs public paths flowchart LR P[Platform] -->|typed MCP| A[Host Agent A] P -->|typed MCP| B[Host Agent B] A |private mesh K3s API / CNI / probes| B Pub[Public client] --> Funnel[public-ingress / Funnel / CF] Funnel --> Gw[Scoped gateway / Ingress] Gw --> W[Workload] Diagram in words: Platform connects to Host Agents over typed MCP; Host Agents reach one another through the private mesh. Public clients reach workloads through public ingress and a scoped gateway. Funnel and Cloudflare public ingress are application north-south paths. They are not substitutes for the private mesh, the Kubernetes datastore, or authenticated Host Agent MCP administration. Tunneling capability opute.capability.tunneling.* owns dedicated host tunnels, probes, removal, and Kubernetes connector install. Dogfood for this site uses a dedicated tunnel opute-www-opute-io — never the Platform tunnel. Stable public hostnames require DNS + TLS readiness probes before calling a surface “done.” Connector run tokens are write-only; MCP clients see [redacted] . Public MCP quick/stable tunnel helpers ( ensure_public_mcp_* ) are separate from Platform admin MCP. Reachability of a marketing hostname is not two-node etcd-quorum HA. Keep those claims separate. Related: Architecture · Recipes · Publish this site · Resources

pages.title: Resources & safety
pages.description: Learn how Host Agent admits resource identities, applies effect gates, enforces quotas, and redacts secrets.
pages.body: Explanation Resources & safety Canonical resource URIs, typed edges, effect gates, quotas, and observation redaction — the fail-closed middle of every tool call. Canonical resource URIs Resources are identified as type:tenant:id (ADR-0003). Tools declare what they Require and Produce as typed edges (ADR-0004). Clients pass admitted URIs; the Host Agent does not invent cluster or guest identity from display labels. flowchart LR Disc[Discovery / list tools] --> URI[Canonical URI] URI --> Admit[Admission] Admit --> Cap[Capacity / quota checks] Cap --> Op[Domain or provider op] Op --> Obs[Typed observation] Obs --> Red[Schema redaction] Red --> Client[MCP client] Diagram in words: Discovery produces a canonical resource URI. Admission and capacity checks precede a typed operation; its observation is schema-redacted before it reaches the MCP client. Effects Catalog entries carry effect classifications such as read , mutation , destructive , and credential_bearing . Standalone mode denies mutations until OPUTE_STANDALONE_ALLOW_MUTATIONS=true . Platform mode applies enrollment policy instead of that env flag. Quotas and storage bounds Incus guest storage quotas are admission concerns (ADR-0010). In-cluster PVC / HA storage bounds are constrained so recipes cannot claim unbounded durability (ADR-0014). Reclaim tools ( prune_unused_cluster_images , garbage_collect_cluster_registry , trim_guest_storage ) are explicit ops — not silent background GC folklore. Redaction (write-only) Schema-marked write-only fields never round-trip through MCP results. Tunnel connector tokens, for example, appear as [redacted] . In-process recipe steps that need those secrets must mint or hold them inside the Host Agent (see dogfood manageHostConnector: true ), not ask an external client to paste them back. flowchart LR Mint[ensure-host-tunnel] --> Tok[runToken writeOnly] Tok --> MCP[MCP result] MCP --> R["[redacted]"] Tok --> InProc[In-process connector install] InProc --> K8s[Kubernetes connector Secret] Diagram in words: A tunnel token is write-only and redacted in the MCP result. The Host Agent can retain it in-process while installing a Kubernetes connector secret. Identity Every Host Agent process carries OPUTE_REMOTE_AGENT_ID . Inventory tools omit caller-supplied host id overrides that would impersonate another agent (ADR-0006). Cross-host mutations target exact opaque agent identities — not Tailscale hostnames or display labels.

Does not enable sparse VHDX. configure_agent_connection Atomically write and remove caller-supplied agent connection environment values, then optionally restart the declared service. configure_local_llm_model LEGACY compatibility wrapper for a local runtime operation; prefer runtime-recipe.v1 configure_local_llm_runtime LEGACY compatibility wrapper for a local runtime operation; prefer runtime-recipe.v1 configure_network Attach a bridged NIC device to a VM so it joins a host network bridge (e.g. wlan0) configure_oci_storage Persist an age-gated OCI image storage budget and optionally prune unused images. configure_service_domain Map a configurable DNS hostname to a Kubernetes Service through Ingress. create_vm Launch a new Incus virtual machine on the host delete_k8s_resource Delete a generic Kubernetes resource from a VM-backed cluster. delete_oci_registry Delete the generic OCI registry namespace and its data resources. delete_postgresql Delete the standalone PostgreSQL namespace and resources. delete_vm Delete a VM forcefully from the host detect_host_platform Detect the operating system and CPU identity of the host running this agent, distinguishing native Windows, macOS, WSL1/WSL2, and native Linux, and reporting the CPU architecture and family including Apple M-series silicon. diagnose_bridge Probes the local bridge control plane (port 9092) and check its health discover_service_ingress Resolve caller-declared service ingress endpoints without product hostname inference. ensure_docker Verify Docker Desktop daemon is running on Windows hosts (does not install Docker Desktop) ensure_host_artifact Download a caller-declared HTTPS artifact into the user's home directory and verify its SHA-256 before installation. ensure_host_file Atomically reconcile a caller-declared managed file; user scope is home-owned and system scope is limited to systemd service units. ensure_host_service_supervisor Ensure the caller-declared host service supervisor is available and persistent; user-scoped services receive an idempotent persistent user-manager contract. ensure_host_tool Ensure an explicitly allowlisted generic host build/runtime tool is installed and available. ensure_local_llm_k3s_proxy LEGACY compatibility wrapper for a local runtime operation; prefer runtime-recipe.v1 ensure_local_llm_relay LEGACY compatibility wrapper for a local runtime operation; prefer runtime-recipe.v1 ensure_local_llm_server_binary LEGACY compatibility wrapper for a local runtime operation; prefer runtime-recipe.v1 ensure_oci_builder Ensure a generic host-side OCI image builder is installed and available. ensure_public_mcp_quick_tunnel Install a pinned cloudflared Quick Tunnel for the Host Agent loopback MCP endpoint and prove authenticated tools/list. The returned trycloudflare.com URL is ephemeral and never a stable production binding. ensure_public_mcp_tunnel Install a pinned cloudflared connector for one provider-issued public MCP binding, store its token in an Opute-owned secret file, and prove authenticated tools/list at the stable HTTPS endpoint. ensure_sqlite_database Provision an isolated caller-scoped SQLite database file. exec_kubernetes_command Execute a kubectl command against a registered cluster using its stored kubeconfig. extract_host_archive Extract a verified caller-declared host archive beneath the user's home directory after rejecting traversal entries. garbage_collect_cluster_registry Delete untagged/unkept in-cluster registry manifests, scale the registry to zero, run registry garbage-collect --delete-untagged, restore, and wait Ready. Default off via includeRegistry. get_capability_catalog Return the immutable authorized capability snapshot and revision used for typed proposals and host plans. get_host_capacity Read provider-neutral host capacity, reservations, pressure, and resource-enforcement state. get_host_info Return host metadata, supported infrastructure operations, and where this Host Agent itself is installed. The agent block answers "where are you, so I can put something next to you?" -- home directory, systemd scope and unit directory, the agent's own environment file, and the loopback MCP endpoint a co-located provider calls back on -- so a recipe can place a provider beside the agent without being told any of it. get_host_plan_run Read the durable status, node results, and revision metadata for a host-plan.v1 run. get_k8s_resource Fetch a Kubernetes resource from a VM-backed cluster as YAML. get_k8s_resource_status Fetch a normalized readiness status for a Kubernetes resource in a VM-backed cluster. get_local_status Return local provider and standalone agent status. get_oci_registry_status Inspect the generic OCI registry deployment inside a VM-backed Kubernetes cluster. get_operation Get a local standalone operation by ID. get_postgresql_service_status Read SQL-gated CloudNativePG PostgreSQL service readiness without returning credentials. get_postgresql_status Inspect the standalone CloudNativePG Cluster. get_runtime_recipe_run Read durable runtime-recipe.v1 provenance and host-plan state. get_sqlite_database_status Inspect an isolated caller-scoped SQLite database file. get_tunnel_run Read durable tunnel-recipe.v1 provenance and host-plan state. get_vm_info Get detailed information and runtime state for an Incus virtual machine inspect_container_storage Inspect runtime-reported image, container, volume, and build-cache storage usage without changing state. inspect_guest_storage Inspect k3s/containerd image, snapshot, and PVC usage inside the bound cluster guest without changing state. Optional registry tag inventory. inspect_host_file Inspect a caller-declared file beneath the current user's home directory without returning its content. inspect_host_service Read systemd service state for a caller-declared host service without changing it. inspect_host_service_supervisor Report whether this scope's service manager will keep caller-owned services running, without changing anything. The read-only counterpart of ensure_host_service_supervisor, and the readiness check a plan node for it requires. inspect_workload Inspect a Kubernetes Deployment and return fields useful for workload forms install_cluster_agent Install and start the Opute cluster agent inside a managed Kubernetes instance so the cluster can report readiness and accept lifecycle work. install_helm_chart Deploy a Helm chart through the K3s Helm Controller on an explicit VM-backed Kubernetes target. The caller's vmName is retained for durable evidence; execution is admitted only through its canonical instance URI. install_incus_stack Install or upgrade Incus, QEMU, virglrenderer, and explicitly requested GPU container prerequisites. install_local_llm_model LEGACY compatibility wrapper for a local runtime operation; prefer runtime-recipe.v1 install_oci_registry Install a generic OCI registry inside a VM-backed Kubernetes cluster. install_postgresql Install a single-node CloudNativePG Cluster in local K3s. CNPG owns credentials. install_provider_tools Validate provider readiness and switch the active infrastructure provider on this host (incus) list_agents Retrieve a consolidated list of all agents (host and cluster) connected to the bridge server. list_certificate_issuers List cert-manager Issuers and ClusterIssuers inside a VM list_configmap_keys List data keys in a Kubernetes ConfigMap inside a VM list_deployments List Kubernetes deployments inside a VM list_host_services List systemd services on the host and return their canonical tenant-scoped resource URIs. list_ingress_classes List Kubernetes ingress classes inside a VM list_k8s_events List bounded, read-only Kubernetes events for an explicit cluster target. list_kubernetes_clusters List all managed Kubernetes clusters (both provisioned by Opute and externally registered). list_local_llm_models LEGACY compatibility wrapper for a local runtime operation; prefer runtime-recipe.v1 list_namespaces List Kubernetes namespaces inside a VM list_operations List local standalone operations. list_pods List Kubernetes pods inside a VM list_secret_keys List data keys in a Kubernetes Secret inside a VM list_services List Kubernetes services inside a VM list_storage_classes List Kubernetes StorageClasses inside a VM list_vms List Incus virtual machines with structured inventory results open_assistant_session Negotiate the bounded assistant-session.v1 contract and bind the client to the current capability revision. opute.provider.install Connect to a trusted provider MCP module, validate its neutral install manifest, execute its selected declarative recipe, and optionally activate the resulting provider generation. opute.provider.reload Load a new trusted provider module generation and reconcile its selected recipe before activation. opute.provider.status Read the connected provider and active provider-generation state without changing host state. opute.provider.teardown Ask the connected provider for a generic teardown host plan, validate it, execute it durably, and retire the provider only after the plan succeeds. opute.provider.validate Run a provider-declared capability validation operation through the generic provider MCP contract. prepare_host_agent_artifacts Build Linux host-agent binaries into a caller-selected directory for platform image builds. probe_gpu_container Launch a disposable Incus system container, probe GPU visibility and NVML, then delete it. probe_http_endpoint Probe a caller-declared HTTP(S) endpoint for provider-neutral reachability evidence. probe_incus_gpu Inspect WSL GPU devices/libraries and host virtualization versions; does not claim container GPU inference success. probe_local_llm LEGACY compatibility wrapper for a local runtime operation; prefer runtime-recipe.v1 probe_openai_compatible_server Probe a caller-declared runtime for model discovery and optional streaming chat readiness. provision_container Launch or reuse a persistent Incus system container with optional GPU, WSL GPU libraries, nesting, and model volume. provision_vm Launch a new Incus instance on the host (system container by default; pass instanceType virtual-machine for a QEMU VM) prune_unused_cluster_images Age-gated removal of unused k3s/containerd images not referenced by current pods. Dry-run first. Never deletes PVCs or Incus instances. put_k8s_secret Create or replace a generic Kubernetes Secret without returning its values. reconcile_host_resource_policy Reconcile an already-authorized versioned host resource policy against one exact host-service URI; raw systemd, cgroup, WSL, and shell controls are not accepted. reconcile_postgresql_service Install or reconcile CloudNativePG and a SQL-gated caller-defined PostgreSQL service in an explicit K3s target. Credentials remain CNPG-owned and are never returned. reconcile_serving_assignment Validate and reconcile a product-neutral serving assignment against an explicit host target. Rejects VM or ambiguous targets and returns bounded readiness evidence. recover_bridge Attempts to recover the local bridge control plane by restarting the service register_kubernetes_cluster Register an externally-managed Kubernetes cluster (not provisioned by Opute). The cluster record is persisted in the bridge database and the kubeconfig is stored on the host. release_postgresql_service_relay Release one caller-owned PostgreSQL service relay without changing the underlying service or databases. remove_host_file Remove one caller-owned regular file beneath the current user's home directory after explicit confirmation and an optional content hash check. remove_local_llm_k3s_proxy LEGACY compatibility wrapper for a local runtime operation; prefer runtime-recipe.v1 remove_local_llm_model LEGACY compatibility wrapper for a local runtime operation; prefer runtime-recipe.v1 remove_local_llm_relay LEGACY compatibility wrapper for a local runtime operation; prefer runtime-recipe.v1 remove_postgresql_service Destructively remove a caller-defined PostgreSQL CNPG service and owned data while preserving the operator. Requires confirm=true. remove_public_mcp_quick_tunnel Stop and remove one Opute-owned Cloudflare Quick Tunnel and its verified artifact after explicit confirmation; unrelated paths are refused. remove_service_domain Remove a configurable Kubernetes service domain mapping. remove_sqlite_database Remove an isolated caller-scoped SQLite database after explicit confirmation. remove_vm_network_device Remove a network interface device from a VM Incus configuration render_helm_template Render a Helm chart to Kubernetes manifests on the host using helm template. request_task_input Pause a read-only task and request one operator response through the standard MCP Tasks input_required/tasks/update flow. reset_incus_stack Fail-closed, ownership-checked, confirmation-gated reset of explicitly selected disposable Incus instances. Returns redacted resumable phase evidence. resize_console Resize an active console terminal on this host. restart_host_service Restart a host-level service such as Incus and verify it becomes active restart_vm Force-stop and then start a VM on the host run_host_command Run a caller-declared bounded host command for a generic serving or infrastructure assignment. run_host_local_recipe Execute a host-recipe.v1 document that declares coordinator=host-agent/mode=local through the durable host-plan runner, so a first cluster node can be established with no Platform in the loop. Read the run with get_host_plan_run. A distributed recipe is refused. run_host_plan Execute an explicit generic host-plan.v1 document with durable idempotency, readiness validation, recovery, and resume state. run_instance_command Execute a provider-declared argv on a resolved Incus VM or system container. The target must be a canonical tenant-scoped URI. run_runtime_recipe Execute an external runtime-recipe.v1 through the durable host-plan runner; with activate=true, validate its neutral serving contract and commit it as the active runtime only after the run succeeds. run_sql Run bounded SQL inside the standalone PostgreSQL pod. run_tunnel_recipe Execute an external tunnel-recipe.v1 through the durable host-plan runner; activate only after generic HTTP exposure validation succeeds. send_console_input Send input data to an active console stream on this host. set_host_service_state Start, stop, restart, enable, or disable a validated host service; user scope is the default. shutdown_wsl Shutdown the complete WSL2 environment through the tested Windows lifecycle capability. Requires explicit destructive approval. stage_build_context Write a caller-provided build context into an allowlisted host directory for build_and_push_oci_image. start_local_llm_runtime LEGACY compatibility wrapper for a local runtime operation; prefer runtime-recipe.v1 start_vm Start a VM on the host stop_local_llm_runtime LEGACY compatibility wrapper for a local runtime operation; prefer runtime-recipe.v1 stop_vm Stop a VM on the host stream_vm_console Stream VM serial console output (lxc console). Direct TTY access for boot observability on this host. terminate_wsl_distribution Terminate exactly one named WSL distribution through the tested Windows interop capability. Requires host approval. trim_guest_storage Run fstrim inside the bound k3s Incus guest after reclaim so unused blocks are punched before VHDX compact. uninstall_incus_stack Purge the Incus virtualization stack from this host. Refuses while any instance remains; opt in to discarding /var/lib/incus. uninstall_provider_tools Remove active provider association from the host after ensuring no VMs remain update_vm_resources Update CPU, memory, and/or root disk limits of an existing VM or system container. Disk is admitted only when the instance's storage pool can enforce it, and is grow-only. validate_host_local_recipe Resolve and validate a host-recipe.v1 document that declares coordinator=host-agent/mode=local, against this Host Agent's catalog and identity, without changing host state. validate_host_plan Validate a generic host-plan.v1 document against the current authorized capability catalog without changing host state. validate_runtime_recipe Resolve and validate an external runtime-recipe.v1 source without changing host state. validate_tunnel_recipe Resolve and validate an external tunnel-recipe.v1 source and its embedded host-plan.v1 without changing host state.
